objects.definition:
#pragma pack(push, 1)

struct TrackElement
{
    WORD Size;        // Size of this structure
    BYTE Type;        // See TrackType
    BOOL FlagDefault; // Set if the track is the default for its TrackType.
    BOOL FlagForced;  // Set if that track MUST be used during playback.
    BOOL FlagLacing;  // Set if the track may contain blocks using lacing.
    UINT MinCache;    // The minimum number of frames a player should be able to cache during playback.
    UINT MaxCache;    // The maximum cache size required to store referenced frames in and the current frame. 0 means no
                      // cache is needed.
    CHAR Language[4]; // Specifies the language of the track, in the ISO-639-2 form. (end with '\0')
};

#pragma pack(pop)
objects.description: Packed structure (1-byte alignment) describing basic properties of a track, including type, default/forced flags, lacing capability, cache hints, and 3-letter ISO-639-2 language code. Callers typically allocate and pass it to ITrackInfo::GetTrackInfo; Size should be set to sizeof(TrackElement) by caller for versioning.

Packed structure (1-byte alignment due to surrounding pragma) with extended properties for video tracks: interlacing, encoded pixel size, display size, display units, and aspect ratio constraints. Typically filled by ITrackInfo::GetTrackExtendedInfo for video tracks; caller should set Size to sizeof(TrackExtendedInfoVideo).

Packed structure (1-byte alignment due to surrounding pragma) with extended properties for audio tracks: sampling frequency, output sampling frequency (eg. SBR), channel count, and bit depth. Typically filled by ITrackInfo::GetTrackExtendedInfo for audio tracks; caller should set Size to sizeof(TrackExtendedInfoAudio).

COM interface (derives from IUnknown, UUID 03E98D51-DDE7-43aa-B70C-42EF84A3A23D) providing access to media track metadata. Methods return counts, fill TrackElement and type-specific extended info structures, and provide codec identifiers and names. Implementations follow COM rules for lifetime; callers manage interface pointers via AddRef/Release. String results are BSTRs allocated by callee; caller typically frees with SysFreeString per COM conventions.

COM interface providing read-only information about internal buffering, likely for a media demuxer/decoder. It exposes buffer count, per-buffer sample/frame count and size in bytes, and the thread priority used for demuxing. UUID is 46070104-1318-4A82-8822-E99AB7CD15C1. Destruction/ownership follows COM conventions via IUnknown (AddRef/Release). Implementation details are not present in this header.

COM interface providing bitrate information. Inherits from IUnknown and exposes two methods returning current and average bit rates as DWORD. The UUID identifies the COM interface. Construction is via COM class objects implementing this interface; this header only declares the interface, not any implementing class. Lifetime is managed via IUnknown reference counting (AddRef/Release).

COM interface for managing a bag of auxiliary resources (name/description/MIME/data/tag). Exposes methods to query count, get/set/append resources, and remove by index or by tag. Inherits from IUnknown and is identified by the specified UUID. Usage follows COM conventions: obtain a pointer via a factory or QueryInterface, manage lifetime with AddRef/Release, and call methods to manipulate the internal collection. Resource payload is arbitrary byte data with associated metadata; ownership and allocation details of returned buffers are not specified in this header.

COM interface (extending IUnknown) for signaling the clean termination of a data segment on a pin. Provides a single method, EndOfSegment, intended to notify downstream components to flush any buffered data before a new segment is started. Lifetime follows COM rules via IUnknown; no additional construction/destruction semantics are defined here.

COM interface extending ISpecifyPropertyPages to allow creation of a specific IPropertyPage instance identified by GUID. It adds a CreatePage method that outputs a property page pointer for the requested page CLSID/GUID. Other behavior is inherited from ISpecifyPropertyPages (not defined here). Destruction/ownership follows COM conventions (reference counting via AddRef/Release).

COM interface for high-level streaming source filters, intended to be exposed by a DirectShow source filter or its output pin. Provides methods to query total stream duration and to request time-based seeking in 100ns DirectShow reference units. Uses REFERENCE_TIME and IUnknown from DirectShow/COM; details of underlying implementation and seeking semantics beyond comments are not defined here.

COM interface extending IUnknown that allows a component (likely a DirectShow source filter) to be instructed to load media from a URL, with optional user-agent and referrer strings. The LoadURL method takes wide-string (OLE) parameters and must be implemented by the filter. No construction details are provided here; instances are typically obtained via COM (e.g., QueryInterface on a filter).

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetRuntimeConfig
functions.description: Enable or disable runtime configuration mode for LAV Video. In runtime mode settings reset to defaults and are not persisted; each call also resets settings to defaults regardless of mode change. Intended for programmatic configuration without touching user registry settings.
requirements: Must be called before LAV Video is connected to other filters.
Do not call during playback; behavior is unspecified/unsupported.
Caller should expect all settings to reset to defaults on each call.
bRuntimeConfig is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetFormatConfiguration
functions.description: Query whether decoding for a specific codec is enabled in LAV Video.
requirements: vCodec must be a valid LAVVideoCodec enumerator; if invalid, the function returns FALSE.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetFormatConfiguration
functions.description: Enable or disable decoding for a specific codec.
requirements: vCodec must be a valid LAVVideoCodec enumerator; invalid codecs result in E_FAIL.
bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetNumThreads
functions.description: Set the number of threads to use for multi‑threaded decoding where supported: 0=Auto (based on CPU cores), 1=single-threaded, >1=explicit thread count.
requirements: dwNum determines threading mode as documented: 0 (auto), 1 (no MT), >1 (multi-threaded).

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetNumThreads
functions.description: Get the configured number of decoding threads: 0=Auto, 1=single-threaded, >1=explicit thread count.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetStreamAR
functions.description: Control which aspect ratio (AR) source is forwarded to the renderer: 0=AR from source filter, 1=AR from the stream, 2=AR from stream if source is not reliable.
requirements: bStreamAR must be one of {0,1,2} as defined.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetStreamAR
functions.description: Get the current aspect ratio source selection: 0=source filter, 1=stream, 2=stream if source unreliable.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetPixelFormat
functions.description: Query whether a specific output pixel format is enabled.
requirements: pixFmt must be a valid LAVOutPixFmts; invalid values return FALSE.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetPixelFormat
functions.description: Enable or disable an output pixel format.
requirements: pixFmt must be a valid LAVOutPixFmts; invalid values result in E_FAIL.
bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetRGBOutputRange
functions.description: Set the RGB output range for YUV→RGB conversion: 0=Auto (match input), 1=Limited (16–235), 2=Full (0–255).
requirements: dwRange must be one of {0,1,2}.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetRGBOutputRange
functions.description: Get the configured RGB output range: 0=Auto, 1=Limited, 2=Full.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDeintFieldOrder
functions.description: Set the deinterlacing field order for the hardware decoder.
requirements: fieldOrder must be a valid LAVDeintFieldOrder value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDeintFieldOrder
functions.description: Get the configured deinterlacing field order for the hardware decoder.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDeintAggressive
functions.description: Deprecated: previously toggled aggressive deinterlacing. Use SetDeinterlacingMode instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; callers should prefer SetDeinterlacingMode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDeintAggressive
functions.description: Deprecated: previously reported aggressive deinterlacing state. Use GetDeinterlacingMode instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; callers should prefer GetDeinterlacingMode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDeintForce
functions.description: Deprecated: previously forced deinterlacing. Use SetDeinterlacingMode instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; callers should prefer SetDeinterlacingMode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDeintForce
functions.description: Deprecated: previously reported forced deinterlacing state. Use GetDeinterlacingMode instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; callers should prefer GetDeinterlacingMode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::CheckHWAccelSupport
functions.description: Check support status for a hardware acceleration type. Returns 0=Unsupported, 1=Supported (libraries present), 2=Currently running.
requirements: Return value semantics: 0 (unsupported), 1 (supported), 2 (currently running).
This typically checks for required libraries/drivers, not full hardware capability.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccel
functions.description: Select the hardware acceleration method to use (see LAVHWAccel).
requirements: hwAccel must be a valid LAVHWAccel enumerator.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccel
functions.description: Get the active hardware acceleration method.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelCodec
functions.description: Enable or disable use of hardware acceleration for a specific codec.
requirements: hwAccelCodec must be a valid LAVVideoHWCodec value.
bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelCodec
functions.description: Query whether a specific codec is configured to use hardware acceleration.
requirements: hwAccelCodec must be a valid LAVVideoHWCodec value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelDeintMode
functions.description: Set the deinterlacing mode used by the hardware decoder.
requirements: deintMode must be a valid LAVHWDeintModes value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelDeintMode
functions.description: Get the deinterlacing mode used by the hardware decoder.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelDeintOutput
functions.description: Set the deinterlacing output cadence for the hardware decoder (FramePerField or FramePer2Field).
requirements: deintOutput must be a valid LAVDeintOutput value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelDeintOutput
functions.description: Get the configured deinterlacing output cadence for the hardware decoder.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelDeintHQ
functions.description: Deprecated: toggles NVIDIA-specific HQ deinterlacing mode (only ever applicable to deprecated CUVID/NVDEC modes).
requirements: Deprecated; NVIDIA HQ deinterlacing is officially deprecated.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelDeintHQ
functions.description: Deprecated: query NVIDIA-specific HQ deinterlacing toggle.
requirements: Deprecated; NVIDIA HQ deinterlacing is officially deprecated.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetSWDeintMode
functions.description: Set the software deinterlacing algorithm (e.g., YADIF, W3FDIF, BWDIF).
requirements: deintMode must be a valid LAVSWDeintModes value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetSWDeintMode
functions.description: Get the configured software deinterlacing algorithm.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetSWDeintOutput
functions.description: Set the output cadence for software deinterlacing (FramePerField or FramePer2Field).
requirements: deintOutput must be a valid LAVDeintOutput value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetSWDeintOutput
functions.description: Get the configured output cadence for software deinterlacing.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDeintTreatAsProgressive
functions.description: Deprecated: previously treated content as progressive to affect deinterlacing. Use SetDeinterlacingMode instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; callers should prefer SetDeinterlacingMode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDeintTreatAsProgressive
functions.description: Deprecated: query 'treat as progressive' deinterlacing setting. Use GetDeinterlacingMode instead.
requirements: Deprecated API; callers should prefer GetDeinterlacingMode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDitherMode
functions.description: Set the dithering mode used during color depth conversion.
requirements: ditherMode must be a valid LAVDitherMode value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDitherMode
functions.description: Get the active dithering mode.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetUseMSWMV9Decoder
functions.description: Enable or disable use of the Microsoft WMV9 DMO Decoder for VC‑1/WMV3 formats.
requirements: bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetUseMSWMV9Decoder
functions.description: Query whether the Microsoft WMV9 DMO Decoder is used for VC‑1/WMV3.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDVDVideoSupport
functions.description: Enable or disable DVD Video support in LAV Video.
requirements: bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDVDVideoSupport
functions.description: Query whether DVD Video support is enabled.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelResolutionFlags
functions.description: Configure which content resolutions are eligible for hardware acceleration using a bitmask of LAVHWResFlag_* flags (SD/HD/UHD).
requirements: dwResFlags must be a bitmask composed of LAVHWResFlag_SD, LAVHWResFlag_HD, and/or LAVHWResFlag_UHD.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelResolutionFlags
functions.description: Get the bitmask of resolution categories eligible for hardware acceleration.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetTrayIcon
functions.description: Enable or disable the LAV Video tray icon.
requirements: bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetTrayIcon
functions.description: Query whether the LAV Video tray icon is enabled.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetDeinterlacingMode
functions.description: Set the overall deinterlacing policy: Auto, Aggressive, Force, or Disable.
requirements: deintMode must be a valid LAVDeintMode value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetDeinterlacingMode
functions.description: Get the current deinterlacing policy.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetGPUDeviceIndex
functions.description: Select the GPU index to use for hardware decoding. Supported only for CUVID and DXVA2 copy‑back; falls back to auto‑detection if invalid. This selection is non‑persistent.
requirements: Must be called before an input is connected to LAV Video.
Only affects CUVID and DXVA2 copy‑back modes.
Device indexing semantics: for CUVID it refers to CUDA‑capable devices; for DXVA2 it includes all D3D9 devices.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelNumDevices
functions.description: Get the number of available devices for the specified hardware acceleration type.
requirements: hwAccel must be a valid LAVHWAccel value.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelDeviceInfo
functions.signature: virtual HRESULT __stdcall ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelDeviceInfo(LAVHWAccel hwAccel, DWORD dwIndex, BSTR *pstrDeviceName, DWORD *pdwDeviceIdentifier) = 0;
functions.description: Retrieve information about a hardware acceleration device by index, returning a device name and an optional device identifier.
requirements: hwAccel must be a valid LAVHWAccel value.
dwIndex should be within the range [0, GetHWAccelNumDevices(hwAccel) - 1].
pstrDeviceName must be a valid writable pointer to receive a BSTR name.
pdwDeviceIdentifier may be NULL if the identifier is not needed; if non-NULL, it must be a valid writable pointer.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::GetHWAccelDeviceIndex
functions.description: Get the selected device index for a given hardware acceleration type; optionally returns its device identifier via pdwDeviceIdentifier.
requirements: hwAccel must be a valid LAVHWAccel value.
pdwDeviceIdentifier may be NULL if the identifier is not needed; if non-NULL, it must be a valid writable pointer.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelDeviceIndex
functions.signature: virtual HRESULT __stdcall ILAVVideoSettings::SetHWAccelDeviceIndex(LAVHWAccel hwAccel, DWORD dwIndex, DWORD dwDeviceIdentifier) = 0;
functions.description: Persistently select the device for a specific hardware acceleration type. The optional dwDeviceIdentifier identifies the device (e.g., device ID); set to 0 if not used.
requirements: hwAccel must be a valid LAVHWAccel value.
dwIndex should reference a valid device as enumerated by GetHWAccelNumDevices/GetHWAccelDeviceInfo.
If not using a device identifier, pass dwDeviceIdentifier=0.
This setting is HW‑accel specific and persistent (contrasts with SetGPUDeviceIndex).

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetH264MVCDecodingOverride
functions.description: Temporarily enable or disable H.264 MVC (stereoscopic) decoding to support features such as 'Play in 2D'. Not persisted.
requirements: This is a temporary, non‑persistent override.
Cannot force‑enable MVC decoding if it is disabled via SetFormatConfiguration.
bEnabled FALSE can temporarily disable MVC decoding even if globally enabled.

functions.name: ILAVVideoSettings::SetEnableCCOutputPin
functions.description: Enable or disable creation of the Closed Caption (CC) output pin.
requirements: bEnabled is a BOOL toggle.

functions.name: ILAVVideoStatus::GetActiveDecoderName
functions.description: Return the name of the currently active decoder, or NULL if no decoder is active.
requirements: Caller must handle a NULL return value (no active decoder).
Returned LPCWSTR is owned by the callee; treat as read‑only.

functions.name: ILAVVideoStatus::GetHWAccelActiveDevice
functions.description: Retrieve the name of the currently active hardware acceleration device as a BSTR.
requirements: pstrDeviceName must be a valid writable pointer for receiving the BSTR.
Caller must follow COM conventions for BSTR allocation/lifetime as returned by the callee (typically SysFreeString when done).

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::SetRuntimeConfig
functions.description: Enable or disable runtime configuration mode for LAV Audio. In runtime mode, all settings are reset to defaults and changes are not persisted, allowing programmatic configuration without affecting user registry settings. Subsequent calls reset settings to defaults again.
requirements: Must not be called during playback; behavior is undocumented if called during playback (per comment).
For smooth operation, call before LAV Audio is connected to other filters (per comment).
The ILAVAudioSettings interface pointer must be a valid, initialized COM object.
Check HRESULT for success/failure.

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::GetDRC
functions.description: Retrieve the Dynamic Range Compression (DRC) state and strength.
requirements: pbDRCEnabled must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the DRC state.
piDRCLevel must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the DRC level (0–100; 100 is maximum).
Check HRESULT for success/failure.

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::SetDRC
functions.description: Enable or disable Dynamic Range Compression and set its strength.
requirements: iDRCLevel must be in the range 0–100 (100 is maximum).
The ILAVAudioSettings interface pointer must be a valid, initialized COM object.
Check HRESULT for success/failure.

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::GetFormatConfiguration
functions.description: Query whether decoding for a specific audio codec is enabled in LAV Audio.
requirements: aCodec must be a valid LAVAudioCodec value for the version in use; if invalid, this function returns FALSE (per comment).
The ILAVAudioSettings interface pointer must be a valid, initialized COM object.
Caller must interpret FALSE as either disabled or invalid codec (per comment).

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::SetFormatConfiguration
functions.description: Enable or disable decoding for a specific audio codec in LAV Audio.
requirements: aCodec must be a valid LAVAudioCodec value for the version in use; if invalid, returns E_FAIL (per comment).
Check HRESULT for success/failure.

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::GetBitstreamConfig
functions.description: Query whether bitstreaming for a specific codec is enabled.
requirements: bsCodec must be a valid LAVBitstreamCodec value; if invalid, this function returns FALSE (per comment).
Caller must interpret FALSE as either disabled or invalid codec (per comment).

functions.name: ILAVAudioSettings::SetBitstreamConfig
functions.description: Enable or disable bitstreaming for a specific codec.
requirements: bsCodec must be a valid LAVBitstreamCodec value; if invalid, returns E_FAIL (per comment).
Check HRESULT for success/failure.

import random
import struct
from typing import List

# Target data type: Windows wide-character (UTF-16LE) string containing a comma-separated
# list of ISO 639-2 language codes. The fuzzers may also pass NULL or empty, but NULL/empty
# are handled by the fuzzer stub via mode. Our buffer backs FUZZ_PARAM_STR(), which is
# converted to std::wstring by naive byte-to-wchar_t widening (assigning 8-bit chars to wchar_t).
# To ensure valid wide content after this widening, we should provide ASCII characters that map
# cleanly to the desired wchar_t values. We will generate ASCII-only strings with commas and
# 3-letter codes, optionally mixed case, optional spaces, and with edge-case patterns to exercise
# parser behavior while remaining valid.

ISO639_2_COMMON = [
    "eng","ger","deu","spa","fra","fre","ita","rus","zho","chi","jpn","kor",
    "por","pol","nld","dut","ara","hin","ben","tur","vie","tha","ukr","ces","cze",
    "ell","gre","heb","fin","nor","swe","dan","isl","hun","ron","rum","slk","slo",
    "srp","hrv","bos","slv","lav","lit","est","msa","may","ind","fil","tgl","cat",
    "eus","baq","glg","gle","iku","tgl","yid","urd","tam","tel","kan","mar","guj",
]

def _random_lang_code(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # 70% pick from common list, 30% craft plausible 3-letter combos
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        code = r.choice(ISO639_2_COMMON)
    else:
        code = ''.join(r.choice('abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz') for _ in range(3))
    # Randomize case with small probability
    if r.random() < 0.2:
        style = r.choice(['upper','title','mixed'])
        if style == 'upper':
            code = code.upper()
        elif style == 'title':
            code = code.title()
        else:
            # Mixed: randomize per char
            code = ''.join(ch.upper() if r.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower() for ch in code)
    return code

def _make_list(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a comma-separated list with interesting spacing and duplicates
    n = r.randint(1, 12)
    codes: List[str] = []
    for i in range(n):
        c = _random_lang_code(r)
        # Occasionally insert duplicates to test dedup logic
        if r.random() < 0.15 and codes:
            c = r.choice(codes)
        # Occasionally insert alternative code variants (e.g., deu/ger)
        if c.lower() == 'ger' and r.random() < 0.5:
            c = 'deu'
        if c.lower() == 'fre' and r.random() < 0.5:
            c = 'fra'
        codes.append(c)
    # Optional spaces around commas
    spacer_modes = ['none','space','mixed']
    mode = r.choice(spacer_modes)
    if mode == 'none':
        sep = ','
        items = codes
    elif mode == 'space':
        sep = ', '
        items = codes
    else:
        # mixed: vary per-separator
        parts = []
        for i, c in enumerate(codes):
            parts.append(c)
            if i != len(codes)-1:
                parts.append(' ' * r.randint(0, 2))
                parts.append(',')
                parts.append(' ' * r.randint(0, 2))
        return ''.join(parts)
    return sep.join(items)

def _edge_case(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # A selection of edge-y but valid lists
    choices = []
    # Single code
    choices.append(_random_lang_code(r))
    # Many codes
    choices.append(','.join(_random_lang_code(r) for _ in range(20)))
    # With spaces and trailing spaces
    choices.append(' , '.join(_random_lang_code(r) for _ in range(r.randint(2,6))))
    # Trailing comma followed by empty elements (still ASCII; consumer may ignore empties)
    # But keep valid-looking by adding a code after empty
    choices.append('eng,,spa')
    # Alternatives for same language
    choices.append('deu,ger')
    choices.append('fra,fre')
    # Mixed case
    choices.append('EnG,SpA,FrA')
    # Duplicates
    choices.append('jpn,jpn,jpn')
    # Longest plausible list under limit
    many = [ _random_lang_code(r) for _ in range(50) ]
    choices.append(','.join(many))
    return r.choice(choices)

def _build_ascii_list(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose between a normal list and an edge-case pattern
    if r.random() < 0.6:
        s = _make_list(r)
    else:
        s = _edge_case(r)
    # Clamp length to avoid exceeding 4096 bytes after UTF-16LE encoding
    max_ascii_len = 2000  # 4000 bytes when widened; leaves room for BOM/terminator if any
    if len(s) > max_ascii_len:
        s = s[:max_ascii_len]
    return s

def _to_utf16le_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-16LE with no BOM, null-terminated to mimic typical wide C-string storage
    b = s.encode('utf-16le')
    # Optionally append NUL terminator 50% of the time (some consumers expect/welcome it)
    # Even if not required, it's valid.
    return b + (b"\x00\x00" if len(b) < 4094 and True else b"")

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)
    # Bias toward providing realistically valid lists; keep ASCII for clean widening
    s = _build_ascii_list(r)
    out = _to_utf16le_bytes(s)
    # Final guard to ensure max size <= 4096
    if len(out) > 4096:
        out = out[:4096 - (4096 % 2)]  # keep even length to not split code units
    return out

    "video/MP2T", "video/quicktime", "video/mp4", "audio/flac",
]

# Edge but valid cases
EDGE_CASES: List[str] = [
    "",              # empty -> some APIs may interpret as reset/none
    "mp4\0",         # embedded NUL in bytes will be kept in std::string length; c_str() adds trailing NUL anyway
    " matroska ",    # with whitespace
    "MATROSKA",      # upper case
    "WebM",          # mixed case
]

# Build a catalog of base candidates
BASE_CANDIDATES: List[str] = COMMON_FORMATS + ALIASES + LONG_IDS + EDGE_CASES


def _random_identifier(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice = rng.randrange(0, 100)
    if choice < 60:
        base = rng.choice(BASE_CANDIDATES)
    elif choice < 85:
        # compose multiple identifiers with random separators
        parts = [rng.choice(COMMON_FORMATS) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 4))]
        sep = rng.choice(SEPARATORS)
        base = sep.join(parts)
    else:
        # generate a plausible custom identifier
        # letters, digits, '-', '/', '.', '+' are typical
        length = rng.randint(3, 24)
        alphabet = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-./+_"
        base = "".join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(length))

    # Optionally add a vendor prefix
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and base:
        base = rng.choice(VENDOR_PREFIXES) + base

    # Optionally vary case
    if base and rng.random() < 0.5:
        base = rng.choice(CASE_FUNCS)(base)

    # Optionally add whitespace padding
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        base = (" " * rng.randint(0, 2)) + base + (" " * rng.randint(0, 2))

    # Truncate to keep overall buffer size small
    return base[:128]


def _ensure_utf8_bytes(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode as UTF-8 without errors; replace if any non-encodable (should not happen with our alphabet)
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='replace')


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Build a set of several identifiers to increase coverage; some fuzzers may
    # reuse the same input buffer for multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR() calls, so include
    # multiple lines/tokens separated by newlines and commas. The stub uses only
    # one std::string per call, but having multiple candidates in one blob allows
    # the fuzzer to slice different substrings if it does tokenization.
    count = rng.randint(1, 6)
    items = []
    for _ in range(count):
        items.append(_random_identifier(rng))

    # Also include a curated block of well-known formats to guarantee coverage
    # irrespective of seed randomness.
    curated = [
        "matroska", "mp4", "mpegts", "avi", "flv", "ogg", "wav", "mp3", "flac",
        "ass", "srt", "dash", "hls", "webm",
    ]
    rng.shuffle(curated)

    # Combine with separators and newlines to keep variety
    blob_parts: List[str] = []
    blob_parts.append(",".join(items))
    blob_parts.append("\n")
    blob_parts.append(",".join(curated[:rng.randint(5, len(curated))]))

    # Optionally append a vendor-prefixed variant line
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        vp = rng.choice(VENDOR_PREFIXES)
        blob_parts.append("\n" + vp + rng.choice(COMMON_FORMATS))

    # Final blob
    blob = "".join(blob_parts)

    # Bound size to <= 4096 bytes
    b = _ensure_utf8_bytes(blob)
    return b[:4096]

# Data type: Windows wide string (UTF-16LE), null-terminated.
# Target stubs consume three wide strings (name, desc, mime) and a data blob (bytes) plus tag numbers.
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR is sourced from the single input buffer; we therefore pack multiple logical fields into one buffer
# and rely on the fuzzer harness to slice them as subsequent FUZZ_PARAM_STR calls.
#
# Encoding format we output:
# [u16le magic = 0x4C41] [u16 count_name_variants]
# Then a sequence of logical records, each consisting of:
#   - Wide string for Name (UTF-16LE, NUL-terminated)
#   - Wide string for Description (UTF-16LE, NUL-terminated)
#   - Wide string for Mime (UTF-16LE, NUL-terminated)
#   - Binary payload length (u32 LE)
#   - Binary payload bytes (len as above, capped)
#   - Two u32 parts composing a tag (low and high)
#
# The fuzzer will call FUZZ_PARAM_STR repeatedly; typical implementations pull subsequent slices from the given buffer.
# By placing multiple plausible triplets and payloads, we give varied, valid inputs.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

# Some curated interesting values for names, descriptions, and MIME types
NAMES = [
    "",
    "logo",
    "thumbnail",
    "cover art",
    "Часть дорожки",
    "字幕",
    "long_name_with_spaces_and_symbols_-_()[]{};,'`~!@#^&+=",
]
DESCS = [
    "",
    "Default resource",
    "High resolution image",
    "Aux data for chapter thumbnails",
    "Описание ресурса с UTF-16",
]
MIMES = [
    "application/octet-stream",
    "text/plain",
    "text/xml",
    "application/json",
    "image/jpeg",
    "image/png",
    "application/pgs",
    "application/x-ass",
]

# Some binary payload patterns
BIN_PATTERNS: List[bytes] = [
    b"\x00",
    b"hello world\n",
    bytes(range(1, 33)),  # 1..32
    b"{\"key\":\"value\"}",
    b"%PDF-1.4\n%\xe2\xe3\xcf\xd3\n",
    b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n" + b"IHDR" + b"\x00" * 16,
]


def _wstr(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Encode to UTF-16LE and add NUL terminator (two zero bytes)
    return s.encode('utf-16le') + b"\x00\x00"


def _rand_lang(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 3-letter ISO-639-2 like strings, sometimes used; keep as part of name variation
    letters = 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz'
    return ''.join(rng.choice(letters) for _ in range(3))


def _make_record(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Pick or synthesize fields
    name = rng.choice(NAMES)
    # Occasionally append language tag or index to name
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        name = f"{name}:{_rand_lang(rng)}" if name else _rand_lang(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        name = name + f"_{rng.randint(0,999)}"

    desc = rng.choice(DESCS)
    mime = rng.choice(MIMES)

    # Construct a payload: choose a pattern and optionally extend with random bytes
    base = rng.choice(BIN_PATTERNS)
    extra_len = rng.randint(0, 128)
    extra = rng.randbytes(extra_len) if extra_len > 0 else b""
    payload = base + extra
    if len(payload) > 1024:
        payload = payload[:1024]
    if len(payload) == 0:
        payload = b"\x00"  # avoid zero-length per stub preference

    # Tag as two u32s to combine into DWORD_PTR in stub
    tag_lo = rng.getrandbits(32)
    tag_hi = rng.getrandbits(32)

    # Assemble
    out = bytearray()
    out += _wstr(name)
    out += _wstr(desc)
    out += _wstr(mime)
    out += struct.pack('<I', len(payload))
    out += payload
    out += struct.pack('<II', tag_lo, tag_hi)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    buf = bytearray()
    # Magic and variant count header
    buf += struct.pack('<H', 0x4C41)  # 'AL' marker

    # Decide how many records to include
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    buf += struct.pack('<H', count)

    for _ in range(count):
        rec = _make_record(rng)
        # Ensure we don't exceed overall limit
        if len(buf) + len(rec) > MAX_TOTAL:
            break
        buf += rec

    # If buffer is very small, pad with another simple record to ensure multiple FUZZ_PARAM_STR slices
    if len(buf) < 128:
        rec = _make_record(rng)
        take = min(len(rec), MAX_TOTAL - len(buf))
        buf += rec[:take]

    return bytes(buf)

# This generator targets IDSMResourceBag::ResSet and ResAppend fuzzers.
# It must provide interesting, valid data for:
# - 3 wide strings (Name, Desc, Mime) created from FUZZ_PARAM_STR()
# - A binary blob used as resource data
# - Two 32-bit integers combined into a 64-bit tag
# The fuzzer calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR multiple times and consumes sequential slices
# from the provided buffer. While we don't control exact slicer semantics, in
# typical libFuzzer-style harnesses FUZZ_PARAM_STR() reads a length-prefixed or
# delimiter-based segment. To maximize valid coverage across calls, we pack a
# small container that concatenates multiple self-descriptive chunks so each
# FUZZ_PARAM_STR can obtain sensible strings and the binary blob can be large
# enough and varied.
#
# Container format (all little-endian):
#   magic: 4 bytes = b'RBAG' (helps early validation in parsers, if any)
#   version: 1 byte = 1
#   count_str: 1 byte = number of following UTF-8 strings (we provide >= 4)
#   For each string i in 0..count_str-1:
#       len_i: 2 bytes
#       bytes: len_i bytes (UTF-8 data; may include commas/spaces)
#   blob_count: 1 byte = number of binary blobs (>=1)
#   For each blob j:
#       blen_j: 2 bytes
#       flags_j: 1 byte (bit0: has Adler32, bit1: is zlib-compressed)
#       data: blen_j bytes (compressed or raw depending on flag1)
#       if has Adler32: 4 bytes of adler32 of the uncompressed/original data
#   tags: two 4-byte unsigned ints (lo, hi) used by fuzzer to form a 64-bit tag
#
# The FUZZ_PARAM_STR consumer will likely just grab slices, but this container
# ensures that wherever it slices, it encounters printable UTF-8 for names/mime
# and rich binary for data, including compressed payloads and checksums.
# Total size kept <= 4096 bytes.

PRINTABLE = (
    "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789-_. "
)

LANGS = [
    "eng", "deu", "fra", "ita", "spa", "jpn", "zho", "kor", "por", "rus",
]

MIMES = [
    "application/octet-stream", "text/plain", "image/png", "image/jpeg",
    "application/json", "video/mp4", "audio/aac", "application/pgs",
]

NAMES = [
    "cover", "poster", "chapters", "license", "subtitle-forced", "font-arial",
    "thumbnails", "artwork-front", "artwork-back", "metadata-extra",
]


def _rand_utf8(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int, bias_words=True) -> bytes:
    # Generate a UTF-8 string, sometimes composed of words and tokens, always printable
    length = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = []
    if bias_words and rng.random() < 0.7:
        # Compose from known tokens to form useful names or MIME-like strings
        choices = []
        choices.append(rng.choice(NAMES))
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            choices.append(rng.choice(LANGS))
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            choices.append(str(rng.randint(1, 9999)))
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            choices.append(rng.choice(["v1", "v2", "final", "draft"]))
        s = "-".join(choices)
        # Ensure length bounds
        if len(s) < length:
            s += " " + "".join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(length - len(s)))
        else:
            s = s[:length]
    else:
        s = "".join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE) for _ in range(length))
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="ignore")


def _rand_mime(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        return rng.choice(MIMES).encode("ascii")
    # Construct a plausible custom MIME
    type_part = rng.choice(["application", "text", "image", "audio", "video"])
    sub = _rand_utf8(rng, 4, 14).decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    sub = "".join(ch for ch in sub if ch.isalnum() or ch in ("-", ".")) or "bin"
    return f"{type_part}/{sub}".encode("ascii", errors="ignore")


def _rand_resource_blob(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> tuple[bytes, int]:
    # Create an interesting binary blob up to target_len bytes
    # Compose small header + patterned data + optional compressed section
    max_len = max(1, target_len)
    modes = ["raw", "pattern", "zlib"]
    mode = rng.choices(modes, weights=[3, 4, 3], k=1)[0]

    if mode == "raw":
        data = rng.randbytes(rng.randint(min(8, max_len), max_len))
        return data[:max_len], 0

    if mode == "pattern":
        chunks = []
        # Header with a simple signature and size
        chunks.append(b"DAT\x00")
        size_field = rng.randint(16, max_len)
        chunks.append(struct.pack("<I", size_field))
        # Repeating motifs
        motifs = [b"\x00\xFF\x00\xFF", b"ABCD", b"\x11\x22\x33\x44", b"\xDE\xAD\xBE\xEF"]
        while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < max_len:
            m = rng.choice(motifs)
            rep = rng.randint(1, 8)
            chunks.append(m * rep)
        data = b"".join(chunks)[:max_len]
        return data, 0

    # zlib compressed random text-like data
    text = _rand_utf8(rng, 64, min(1024, max_len * 2)).decode("utf-8", errors="ignore")
    # Add some JSON-like structure to be meaningful for consumers
    j = {
        "name": rng.choice(NAMES),
        "lang": rng.choice(LANGS),
        "mime": _rand_mime(rng).decode("ascii", errors="ignore"),
        "size": rng.randint(1, 1_000_000),
        "flags": rng.randint(0, 0xFFFF),
        "note": text,
    }
    payload = ("{" + ", ".join(f"\"{k}\": \"{str(v)}\"" for k, v in j.items()) + "}").encode("utf-8")
    try:
        comp = zlib.compress(payload, level=rng.randint(1, 9))
        if len(comp) > max_len:
            comp = comp[:max_len]
        return comp, 2  # flag bit1 indicates zlib-compressed
    except Exception:
        data = payload[:max_len] or b"x"
        return data, 0


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide counts
    count_str = rng.randint(4, 8)  # enough for Name, Desc, Mime, plus extras
    blob_count = rng.randint(1, 3)

    # Start building the container
    parts = []
    parts.append(b"RBAG")
    parts.append(struct.pack("<B", 1))  # version
    parts.append(struct.pack("<B", count_str))

    # First three strings: name, desc, mime are biased accordingly
    name_b = _rand_utf8(rng, 5, 24)
    desc_b = _rand_utf8(rng, 10, 60)
    mime_b = _rand_mime(rng)

    strings = [name_b, desc_b, mime_b]
    # Additional strings: random useful tokens
    for _ in range(count_str - 3):
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            strings.append(_rand_mime(rng))
        else:
            strings.append(_rand_utf8(rng, 4, 32))

    # Serialize strings with 2-byte lengths
    for s in strings:
        s = s[:65535]
        parts.append(struct.pack("<H", len(s)))
        parts.append(s)

    # Blobs
    parts.append(struct.pack("<B", blob_count))
    total_size_cap = 4096
    current_size = sum(len(p) for p in parts)
    remaining = max(0, total_size_cap - current_size - blob_count * (2 + 1 + 4 + 0))

    # Distribute remaining among blobs
    lens = []
    if blob_count == 1:
        lens = [max(1, min(1024, remaining))]
    else:
        for i in range(blob_count):
            piece = max(1, min(768, remaining // (blob_count - i) if (blob_count - i) > 0 else remaining))
            lens.append(piece)
            remaining -= piece

    for L in lens:
        data, flag = _rand_resource_blob(rng, max(1, L))
        # Optional checksum flag
        has_adler = 1 if rng.random() < 0.5 else 0
        flags = (has_adler << 0) | (flag << 1)
        parts.append(struct.pack("<H", len(data)))
        parts.append(struct.pack("<B", flags))
        parts.append(data)
        if has_adler:
            # Compute adler of uncompressed data when possible; we don't retain original separately
            ad = zlib.adler32(data) & 0xFFFFFFFF
            parts.append(struct.pack("<I", ad))

    # Two 32-bit values for tag building in the stub
    lo = rng.getrandbits(32)
    hi = rng.getrandbits(32)
    parts.append(struct.pack("<II", lo, hi))

    out = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure non-empty and within cap
    if not out:
        out = b"RBAG\x01\x03\x00\x00"
    return out[:4096]

def _rand_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:

        drive = rng.choice(['C', 'D', 'E'])

        ]

def _widen_ansi_to_utf16le_z(s: str) -> bytes:
    # Best-effort: zero-extend each byte to UTF-16LE code unit and add NUL terminator.
    b = s.encode('latin1', errors='replace')
    # Map bytes to UTF-16LE code units
    out = bytearray()
    for by in b:
        out.append(by)
        out.append(0)
    # NUL terminator (UTF-16LE)
    out.append(0)
    out.append(0)
    return bytes(out)

def _build_packet(url_utf8: str, ua_utf8: str | None, ref_utf8: str | None) -> bytes:
    # Simple length-prefixed container:
    # [u32 len_url][len_url bytes utf8][u32 len_ua][ua bytes][u32 len_ref][ref bytes]
    # Fuzzer stub reads FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME for path; FUZZ_PARAM_STR for UA/ref host.
    # Here we supply complete strings so a harness can split if desired.
    def u32(n: int) -> bytes:
        return int(n & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little')
    ua_bytes = (ua_utf8.encode('utf-8') if ua_utf8 is not None else b"")
    ref_bytes = (ref_utf8.encode('utf-8') if ref_utf8 is not None else b"")
    url_bytes = url_utf8.encode('utf-8')
    blob = bytearray()
    blob += u32(len(url_bytes)) + url_bytes
    blob += u32(len(ua_bytes)) + ua_bytes
    blob += u32(len(ref_bytes)) + ref_bytes
    return bytes(blob)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # 1) Construct file URL
    path = _rand_filename(rng)
    url_utf8 = "file:///" + path

    # 2) Optionally construct User-Agent (~66% chance)
    ua_utf8: str | None
    if rng.random() < 2/3:
        base = rng.choice([
            "FuzzUA/1.0", "FuzzUA/2.1", "LavFuzz/0.1", "libavfuzz/5.0", "TestHarness/9.9"
        ])
        tail = _rand_ascii(rng, 0, 32)
        ua_utf8 = base + (" " + tail if tail else "")
    else:
        ua_utf8 = None

    # 3) Optionally construct Referrer (~33% chance)
    ref_utf8: str | None
    if rng.random() < 1/3:
        host_raw = _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 24)
        host = _sanitize_host(host_raw)
        ref_utf8 = f"https://{host}.test/"
    else:
        ref_utf8 = None

    # 4) Build a compact, self-describing blob for harnesses that multiplex FUZZ_PARAMs
    packet = _build_packet(url_utf8, ua_utf8, ref_utf8)

    # 5) Also append UTF-16LE zero-terminated copies to directly feed LPCOLESTR if desired
    # Layout after packet:
    # [u32 wurl_len][wurl bytes utf16le incl NUL][u32 wua_len][wua utf16le or 0][u32 wref_len][wref utf16le or 0]
    def u32(n: int) -> bytes:
        return int(n & 0xFFFFFFFF).to_bytes(4, 'little')

    wurl = _widen_ansi_to_utf16le_z(url_utf8)
    wua = _widen_ansi_to_utf16le_z(ua_utf8) if ua_utf8 is not None else b"\x00\x00"
    wref = _widen_ansi_to_utf16le_z(ref_utf8) if ref_utf8 is not None else b"\x00\x00"

    tail = bytearray()
    tail += u32(len(wurl)) + wurl
    tail += u32(len(wua)) + wua
    tail += u32(len(wref)) + wref

    out = packet + bytes(tail)

    # Ensure we do not exceed 4096 bytes
    return out[:4096]

import os
import random
import string
from typing import List

# Data type: HTTP user-agent string (optional wide string); also used to form referrer host
# Fuzzer stub behavior summary:
# - FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME(): framework creates a real temp file from these bytes; stub converts to file:/// URL
# - FUZZ_PARAM_STR(): used to build User-Agent suffix and Referrer host; stub sanitizes host to [A-Za-z0-9-.]
# Goal: Produce valid, interesting data that exercises code paths with:
#   * Reasonable file paths (ASCII and some unicode-ish bytes) so file:/// URL is valid
#   * Concise, varied UA tokens
#   * Host-like strings that become valid after sanitization
# Constraints: return <=4096 bytes; no external I/O

SAFE_ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-._/\\ "
HOST_SAFE = string.ascii_lowercase + string.digits + "-."

def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]):
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]

def _make_windows_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build paths like C:\Users\fuzz\AppData\Local\Temp\fz_<rand>.bin
    drive = _rand_choice(rng, list(string.ascii_uppercase)) + ":"
    parts = [
        drive,
        "\\",
        _rand_choice(rng, ["Temp", "Users", "Windows", "ProgramData", "fuzz", "t"]),
    ]
    n_extra = rng.randint(1, 4)
    for _ in range(n_extra):
        seg = _segment_name(rng, allow_unicode=True)
        parts += ["\\", seg]
    leaf = _leaf_filename(rng)
    parts += ["\\", leaf]
    return "".join(parts)

def _make_unix_path(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build paths like /tmp/fz/<rand>/<file>
    root = _rand_choice(rng, ["/tmp", "/var/tmp", "/home/fuzz", "/"])
    parts = [root]
    n_extra = rng.randint(0, 3)
    for _ in range(n_extra):
        parts.append(_segment_name(rng, allow_unicode=True))
    parts.append(_leaf_filename(rng))
    return "/".join([p.strip("/") for p in parts]).replace("//", "/") if root != "/" else "/" + "/".join(parts[1:])

def _segment_name(rng: random.Random, allow_unicode: bool) -> str:
    base = []
    length = rng.randint(1, 12)
    for _ in range(length):
        if allow_unicode and rng.random() < 0.15:
            # Insert a byte > 0x7F, which stub zero-extends into WCHAR; keep within BMP ASCII-ish
            base.append(chr(rng.randint(0x80, 0xFF)))
        else:
            base.append(_rand_choice(rng, list(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_")))
    return "".join(base)

def _leaf_filename(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    name = _segment_name(rng, allow_unicode=True)
    ext = _rand_choice(rng, [".bin", ".dat", ".mp4", ".mkv", ".h264", ".aac", ".raw", ""])
    return name + ext

def _make_user_agent_suffix(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Keep UA concise (stub trims to 128). Mix tokens to be realistic
    tokens = [
        "Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64",
        "X11; Linux x86_64",
        "Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7",
        "Android 13",
        "iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 16_5 like Mac OS X",
        "rv:109.0",
        "AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko)",
        "Gecko/20100101",
        "Chrome/118.0.0.0",
        "Safari/537.36",
        "Edge/118.0",
    ]
    # Randomly compose 1-3 tokens
    parts = []
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, tokens))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, tokens))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        parts.append(_rand_choice(rng, tokens))
    # Add a short fuzz token to vary
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        fuzz_len = rng.randint(3, 10)
        fuzz_token = ''.join(_rand_choice(rng, list(string.ascii_letters + string.digits)) for _ in range(fuzz_len))
        parts.append(fuzz_token)
    ua = "; ".join(parts)
    if not ua:
        ua = "Generic/1.0"
    # Prefix FuzzUA/ per stub convention
    full = f"FuzzUA/{ua}"
    return full[:128]

def _make_host_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Produce a host that, after stub sanitization, becomes valid
    labels = []
    nlabels = rng.randint(1, 3)
    for _ in range(nlabels):
        l = rng.randint(1, 10)
        lab = []
        for _ in range(l):
            if rng.random() < 0.2:
                # include chars that will be mapped to 'a' by stub
                lab.append(_rand_choice(rng, list("_!*@$%+/:;[]{}")))
            else:
                lab.append(_rand_choice(rng, list(HOST_SAFE)))
        # ensure label doesn't start/end with '-'
        s = ''.join(lab).strip('-')
        if not s:
            s = 'a'
        labels.append(s)
    host = '.'.join(labels)
    # Limit to 48 (stub trims), but we build shorter
    return host[:40]

def _build_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose three logical sections separated by newlines, so FUZZ_PARAM_STR() can pull a slice
    # 1) UA suggestion line
    ua = _make_user_agent_suffix(rng)
    # 2) Host suggestion line
    host = _make_host_like(rng)
    # 3) Path suggestion line (platform-random)
    path = _make_windows_path(rng) if rng.random() < 0.5 else _make_unix_path(rng)

    # Shuffle lines to increase variability in which FUZZ_PARAM_STR reads
    lines = [ua, host, path]
    rng.shuffle(lines)

    blob = "\n".join(lines)
    # Ensure size constraint
    b = blob.encode('latin1', errors='ignore')[:4000]
    # Add a small random trailer to diversify
    if len(b) < 4096 and rng.random() < 0.5:
        extra_len = rng.randint(0, min(128, 4096 - len(b)))
        extra = bytes(rng.randrange(32, 127) for _ in range(extra_len))
        b += extra
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    payload = _build_payload(rng)
    # Guarantee non-empty to satisfy path requirement in stub
    if not payload:
        payload = b"FuzzUA/Generic\nexample\n/tmp/fz.dat"
    return payload
